subject: history
title: The Black Death 1346-1353
welcome_lead: Trace the deadliest pandemic in recorded history as it swept from Central Asia through the Mediterranean and across Europe.
meta_desc: History Society & Economy 750-1400 Adventure 2: the Black Death, its spread and social-economic consequences.
final_note: You have walked the plague routes. Demographic collapse reshaped wages, religion and rebellion across Eurasia.

concepts.def: Bacterium identified as the principal cause of plague, transmitted by fleas on rodents.
Form of plague producing swollen lymph nodes (buboes) and the highest case load during the pandemic.
Lung-based plague spread directly between humans by respiratory droplets, almost always fatal without treatment.
Religious movement of penitents who whipped themselves publicly in the hope of averting divine wrath.
English law attempting to cap wages at pre-plague levels in response to labour shortages.
English uprising partly rooted in long-term consequences of the Black Death and resentment of poll taxes.

walkthroughs.body_html: The pandemic reached Caffa in Crimea by 1346, allegedly catapulted into the city by besieging Mongol forces. Genoese ships carried the disease to Sicily in 1347; from there it leapt across the Mediterranean to North Africa and through Iberia, Italy, France, England (1348-49) and into Scandinavia and Russia by 1351-53.

Modern estimates suggest that between a third and half of Europe's population — perhaps 25 to 50 million people — died within a few years. Some towns and monasteries effectively ceased to exist. Recurrent outbreaks across the later fourteenth and fifteenth centuries prevented quick recovery and reshaped settlement patterns.

Labour scarcity drove wages up and rents down, threatening landlord incomes. Governments tried to legislate restraint (Statute of Labourers, 1351; French ordinances of 1351). Religious responses included flagellant movements, anti-Jewish pogroms in the Rhineland and an intensified concern with death seen in macabre art such as the Danse Macabre.
